description: The FastAPI service from every side, on OpenTelemetry metrics.

panels.description: Requests per second now, and how it moved over the range.
panels.title: RPS

panels.description: Share of server errors now. Orange above 1% · red above 5%.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route", http_response_status_code=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / sum(rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: 5xx ratio

panels.description: 95th percentile of request duration now. Orange above 500 ms · red above 1 s.
panels.title: P95 latency

panels.description:
Application Performance Index over the last 5 minutes, and how it moved over the range, 0–1: satisfied below the `Apdex: satisfied` threshold, tolerating up to `Apdex: tolerated` (count as half), frustrated above.

≥ 0.94 excellent · ≥ 0.7 acceptable · < 0.7 poor

targets.expr: (sum(increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route", le="$satisfied"}[5m])) + sum(increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route", le="$tolerated"}[5m]))) / 2 / sum(increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[5m]))

panels.title: Apdex

panels.description: Hosts serving the application — a container in Compose, a pod in Kubernetes: the `host_name` of `target_info`. A dip is a restart.
panels.title: Instances

panels.description: Serving processes across all instances, each with its own `service.instance.id` — the `instance` label. A dip is a worker replaced.
panels.title: Workers

panels.description: Every route over the selected range: its traffic trend, requests, share of 2xx, 3xx, 4xx and 5xx, mean duration, P50, P95 and P99. A mean far below P95 means a long tail. Click a route to narrow the dashboard to it, or for its traces.

targets.expr: (sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route", http_response_status_code=~"5.."}[$__range])) or sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range])) * 0) / sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range]))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (http_route, le) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range])))

sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range])) / sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range]))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (http_route, le) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range])))

(sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route", http_response_status_code=~"4.."}[$__range])) or sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range])) * 0) / sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range]))

(sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route", http_response_status_code=~"2.."}[$__range])) or sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range])) * 0) / sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range]))

(sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route", http_response_status_code=~"3.."}[$__range])) or sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range])) * 0) / sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range]))
histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (http_route, le) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__range])))

panels.title: Routes

panels.description: Requests per second per route; the white line is the total, the grey dashed one the total at the same time yesterday.
panels.title: RPS — total · by route

panels.description: The classes picked in `Status codes`: a thick line per class, its total — 2xx green · 3xx blue · 4xx dashed orange · 5xx red — and a thin one per route and code. With 2xx picked, 2xx sets the scale. Click a series for its traces.

value.title: Traces of this route with this code
Traces with a code of this class

panels.title: RPS by status code — total · by route

panels.description: The percentiles picked in `Route percentiles`: a thick line per percentile across all routes — P50 blue, P95 white, P99 purple — a grey dashed one for it yesterday, and a thin one per route; above 500 ms the zone is orange, above 1 s red. Click a route's line for its traces.

targets.expr: label_map(histogram_quantiles("phi", ${quantiles:csv}, sum by (le) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__rate_interval] offset 1d))), "phi", "0.5", "p50", "0.95", "p95", "0.99", "p99")

panels.title: Latency ${quantiles:text} — total · by route

panels.description: How many requests finished in each duration bucket over time: the darker the cell, the more requests. The tail is the pale cells high above the bulk — what P99 above sums up in one line.
panels.title: Latency — distribution

panels.description: Unhandled exceptions from the access log, one series per route and type — /api/fail · RuntimeError. The legend lists the first 8; the eye filters the rest by route or type. Messages and counts are beside.

links.title: Lines with this exception on this route
Traces with this exception on this route

targets.expr: sum by (route, error_type) (count_over_time({service_name="$service"} | json | error_type!="" | route=~"$route" [$__interval]))

panels.title: Exceptions — by route and type

panels.description: Every exception over the selected range: its type, route and message, most frequent first. Click a message for its log lines and their stacks.

targets.expr: sum by (error_type, route, error_message) (count_over_time({service_name="$service"} | json | error_type!="" | route=~"$route" [$__range]))

panels.title: Exceptions — messages

panels.description: Request and response bodies. Received counts only requests with a body and a `Content-Length` header.
panels.title: Bytes per second — received · sent

panels.description: 95th percentile of the body per route, of requests and of responses. Only requests with a body are measured: here, `POST /api/posts`.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (http_request_method, http_route, le) (rate(http_server_request_body_size_bytes_bucket{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__rate_interval])))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (http_request_method, http_route, le) (rate(http_server_response_body_size_bytes_bucket{job=~"$service", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Body size P95 — request · response, by route

panels.description: Share of the 7-day budget of 5xx still unspent, for an availability target of `$slo`. At zero the target is missed.
panels.title: Error budget left — 7 days

panels.description: How fast the 7-day error budget burns: 1× spends it exactly in 7 days. Red at 3.36× over 1 h (2% of the budget in an hour) and 1.4× over 6 h (5% in six hours).
panels.title: Burn rate — 1 h · 6 h

panels.description: Share of requests over the last 7 days that finished within the `Apdex: satisfied` threshold — the latency objective beside the availability one, for the whole service like the budget.
panels.title: Fast enough — 7 days

panels.description: Share of requests not answered with 5xx, against the availability target `$slo`: the red zone under the dashed line is below the target.
panels.title: Availability — vs objective

panels.description: Each worker's share of the requests. The dashed line is an even split: a worker far from it is starved or overloaded.

targets.expr: sum by (instance) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", instance=~"(${host:regex})-[0-9]+", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__rate_interval])) / scalar(sum(rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$service", instance=~"(${host:regex})-[0-9]+", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Request share — by worker

panels.description: The percentiles picked in `Worker percentiles`, per worker under a thick total — P50 blue, P95 white, P99 purple: one worker slower than the rest is hidden in the total.

targets.expr: label_map(histogram_quantiles("phi", ${worker_quantiles:csv}, sum by (instance, le) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$service", instance=~"(${host:regex})-[0-9]+", http_request_method=~"$method", http_route=~"$route"}[$__rate_interval]))), "phi", "0.5", "p50", "0.95", "p95", "0.99", "p99")

panels.title: Latency ${worker_quantiles:text} — total · by worker

panels.description: Requests being handled right now, stacked by worker: the top is the total, expected ≈ RPS × mean duration (Little's law). The OpenTelemetry gauge has no route label.
panels.title: In flight — by worker

panels.description: CPU time per second of each worker. The GIL holds a Python worker to about one core: orange from 80%, red at 100% — saturated however idle the host is.
panels.title: CPU — by worker, one core is 100%

panels.description: How often the kernel takes the CPU away from a worker mid-work. A rise means workers compete for the CPU.
panels.title: Involuntary context switches — by worker

panels.description: Workers that appeared in each minute: a deploy, a crash or a recycle. A steady trickle with no deploy behind it is a worker dying.

targets.expr: (count(count by (instance) (process_thread_count{job=~"$service", instance=~"(${host:regex})-[0-9]+"}) unless count by (instance) (process_thread_count{job=~"$service", instance=~"(${host:regex})-[0-9]+"} offset 1m))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Worker starts — per minute

panels.description: Resident memory of each worker process. A line that only climbs is a leak.
panels.title: Memory — by worker

panels.description: Threads of each worker: the event loop, the exporters, gRPC and the profiler.
panels.title: Threads — by worker

panels.description: Sockets and files each worker holds open.
panels.title: Open file descriptors — by worker

panels.description: CPython's garbage collector runs per second, all workers together.
panels.title: GC collections — by generation

panels.description: `count primes` from /api/cpu and /api/report is the widest frame here.
panels.title: CPU profile — flame graph

panels.description: The traces picked in `Traces shown`: slower than the `Slow trace` threshold, failed, either, or all, newest first. Open one: from a span to its log lines, its profile and the metrics of its operation.

targets.query: {resource.service.name="$service" && kind=server && span.http.request.method=~"${method:pipe}" && span.http.route=~"${route:pipe}" && ("all" = "$shown" || ("slow" =~ "$shown" && duration > $slow) || ("failed" =~ "$shown" && status = error))} with(most_recent=true)

panels.title: Traces — ${shown:text}

panels.description: Time, level, status, duration, request and message, each in its column. Open a line for all its fields: `trace_id` leads to the trace, `request_id` to every line of the request.

targets.expr: {service_name="$service", lvl=~"${levels:regex}"} | json | label_format request=`{{if .path}}{{.method}} {{.path}}{{if .query}}?{{.query}}{{end}}{{end}}`, took=`{{if .duration_ms}}{{.duration_ms}} ms{{end}}` | line_format "{{.msg}}{{if .error_type}} — {{.error_type}}: {{.error_message}}{{end}}"
